Hmmm, didn't think to post about these types of stocks before. Iriko-dashi is made from dried anchovies.

Dashi is a Japanese for soup stock. There are several wonderfully simple dashi that are even an absolute beginner can create and enjoy. I find many are intimidated by more complex stocks where failure to skim and strain properly can really negatively impact taste. Not so with these types of soup stocks.

You can make various kinds of dashi with the following ingredients:

  • Dried fish ( such as Iriko or bonito)
  • Dried Mushrooms
  • Dried Kelp (Konbu)
  • Shrimp shells

You just soak your primary ingredient overnight in water. Next day, slowly bring to boil, skim the foam that is released, simmer for 8-10 minutes, strain and you have stock.

Sometimes using things like kelp, you might remove it before boiling to change strength of flavor. With the dried fish, I remove heads and stomachs for a milder flavor with less chance of turning bitter.

These stocks can be used as is or a base to make more flavorful broths and soups. We are going to make finger noodles at my house so this stock will be used to make the soup for that adventure.
